3. The petitioner-Bank as defendant entered appearance in the said suit on 05.3.2007 and thereafter, the petitioner-Bank filed an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 11.4.2007 for rejection of the plaint contending, inter-alia, that the transaction as contemplated under the suit is not a debt (FY) as defined in section 2 of the Ain, 2003 and the suit is also hopelessly barred by the law of limitation. 

 8. Mr. Arshadur Rouf further submits that the purpose of the Ain, 2003 is to recover of debt (ঋণ) of the banks and financial institutions named therein from the defaulter borrowers and in this case there is no bank and customer relationship between the two schedule banks and in view of the provisions of the Ain, 2003 the Artha Rin Adalat has got no jurisdiction to deal with the matter other than to recovery of debt (vet) and in that view of the matter the respondent NO.1, Artha Rin Adalat ought to have allowed the application for rejection of the plaint of the petitioner. Mr. Arshadur Rouf also submits that respondent No.2, Marcantile Bank Ltd. filed the Suit for recovery of overdue interest for the period between 12.08.2001 and 09.11.2006 long after 5 years 4 months in spite of fact that the claim of the respondent No.2 became payable on 12.08.2001 and in that view of the matter the suit is barred by limitation. Mr. Arshadur Rouf finally submits that the petitioner appeared in the suit on 05.03.2007 and submitted the written statement on 03.05.2007 within the period prescribed by the Ain, 2003 and therefore, there is no scope to found the petitioner-bank as defaulter and fixing costs of Tk. 2000.00 on the petitioner for failure to submit the written statement within time prescribed by law and as such the impugned order dated 17.05.2007 passed by the respondent No.1 is illegal and malafide and hence the same is liable to be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 11. The petitioner-Bank appeared in the suit and filed an application under Order VII Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint mainly on 2(two) counts that : (i) the amount claimed by the plaintiff bank is not loan (list) within the meaning of section 2(ga) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 as the transaction between the petitioner-bank and respondent-bank is completely a business and commercial transaction between the two schedule banks and not related to recovery of debt OM) and (ii) the suit was hopelessly barred by the law of limitation inasmuch the respondent-Bank did file the suit within 3(three) years. The respondent No.1, Artha Rin Adalat No.2, Dhaka rejected the application stating as follows: 

 17. The contentions as raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the nature of transaction between the petitioner-bank and respondent No.2 is completely a business and commercial transaction between the two schedule banks and not related to recovery of debt and the same cannot be treated as "loan OM) as defined in section 2(ga) of the Ain, 2003 and the Artha Rin Adalat traveled beyond its jurisdiction in entertaining such suit as the Adalat has got no jurisdiction to deal with the matter other than to recovery of debt (ঋণ) does not appear to be without substance. In any view of the matter, having regard to the facts as aforesaid, we are inclined to direct the Artha Rin Adalat to decide the points upon framing issues as to whether the amount claimed by the plaintiff-bank against the defendant-bank does come within the definition of loan (ঋণ) as provided in section 2(ga) of the Ain, 2003 and the suit is barred by the law of limitation.
